questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Elements whose molecules normally exist as two atoms joined together, such as H₂, O₂, N₂ and Cl₂, are described as
questions.explanation: Two identical atoms walk through chemistry hand in hand.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into useful nitrogen compounds, whether by bacteria in root nodules or by industry, is called
questions.explanation: The free gas of the air is locked into compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The fertiliser made by treating ground phosphate rock with sulphuric acid, so that the phosphorus becomes soluble and available to plants, is
questions.explanation: The acid makes the rock's phosphorus drinkable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A white powder made by the action of chlorine on slaked lime, used to kill germs in treated water, is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The law stating that the rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its density is
questions.explanation: Light gases race where heavy gases crawl.

questions.q: The fuel gas mixture of carbon(II) oxide and nitrogen, made by passing air over hot coke, is

questions.q: The radioactive metal whose atoms can be split in a reactor to release enormous energy is

questions.q: The method of finding the age of very old remains by measuring the amount of carbon-14 still left in them is called

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The law stating that when gases react, the volumes of the reacting gases and the gaseous products bear simple whole-number ratios to one another is
questions.explanation: One volume plus two volumes gives two volumes of steam.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The process of heating a sulphide ore strongly in excess air so that it is converted to the metal oxide is called

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The process of heating a carbonate ore strongly in a limited supply of air, or none at all, so that it breaks down to the oxide is called
questions.explanation: The carbonate lets its carbon dioxide escape.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the laboratory, ammonia is prepared by gently heating a mixture of ammonium chloride and calcium hydroxide (slaked lime). The gas is collected by
questions.A: downward delivery, since it is lighter than air
questions.B: upward delivery, since it is heavier than air
questions.D: in a sealed jar with a tap at once
questions.explanation: The light gas rises and pushes the air out below.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The theory which explains the behaviour of matter by picturing it as made of tiny particles in constant motion, with strong forces in solids and almost none in gases, is the
questions.explanation: Everything is particles, and the particles move.

questions.q: The process of removing dissolved salts from sea water to obtain fresh water, as done in some coastal desert cities, is called
